# B8 — Monitoring Runbook (static)

**Status:** ✅ Implemented (Phase 1) · **Jira:** [SCRUM-XX / B8](https://modeo-team-1.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-XX) · **Feeds:** Ops (G3/G4 + steady state) · **Code:** `src/macro_pipeline/observability.py`, `src/macro_pipeline/dashboard.py`, `scripts/build_monitoring.py`

The all-free, file-based monitoring stack (PRD §397). This file is the **static human
runbook**: what each signal means and how to operate it. `scripts/build_monitoring.py`
**appends it verbatim** under the live, auto-generated dashboard to produce
`docs/monitoring.md` — so read `docs/monitoring.md` top-to-bottom: numbers first, then this.

> The generator owns `docs/monitoring.md`. **Do not hand-edit it** — edit *this* file (the
> prose) or the data files (the numbers), then regenerate.

## The cardinal rule — 🔴 red widget ⇒ cron pauses

PRD §397's most consequential widget is **validator pass rate per O-check**, with the two
non-negotiable checks highlighted RED if `< 100%`:

| Critical check | What it is | Why it's launch-blocking |
|---|---|---|
| `O5` | number grounding (== eval criterion **C2**) | a fabricated/ungrounded number is the worst failure mode — Bruce quotes these |
| `O8` | banned-phrase scan | last-mile defense against advice-y / partisan framing (PRD content-safety) |

`build_metrics` sets `red = True` when the fallback rate exceeds 50%. A critical check
(O5/O8) below 100% sets `warn = True` instead — **AMBER**: alert, but keep publishing, because
the validator caught it and that run already served the safe fallback card (amended 2026-08-26;
the old "any critical check < 100% ⇒ red" rule latched a 30-day publish freeze on a single
caught O5). When red,
`scripts/build_monitoring.py` prints `STATUS: RED` and **exits 3**. A future cron step gates
on that exit code: **red ⇒ pause the cron** until a human triages (don't ship more briefings
on top of a number-grounding regression). Green ⇒ exit 0, business as usual.

> **Delivered in B8:** the red gate, the `exit 3` signal, and the healthcheck/alert API.
> **Wired by B6** (`scripts/run_daily.py` + `.github/workflows/daily-briefing.yml`, see
> [`docs/cron-b6.md`](cron-b6.md)): the scheduled entrypoint now *consumes* `exit 3` to actually
> pause publication (the gate step exits 1 without committing, so the PWA keeps last-good), and
> brackets the run with the `start`/`success`/`fail` healthcheck pings. B8 ships the mechanism;
> B6 wired it to the trigger. (The live run on a real device is B9.)

## Signals at a glance

| Signal | Source | Lives in | Read it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Per-run audit | `observability.log_run` | `logs/runs.jsonl` (tracked, indefinite retention) | every briefing: input hash, source, validator status + failed checks, model, prompt version, latency, llm_calls |
| Validator pass rate / O-check | `dashboard.aggregate_runs` | `docs/monitoring.md` table | the red widget (C2/O5 + O8); per-check `n` |
| Latency p50 / p95 | run records `latency_ms` | `docs/monitoring.md` | LLM-call slowness trend |
| Fallback rate | run records `source` | `docs/monitoring.md` | quality degradation (refusals are **excluded** from the numerator — a correct data-bail is not a fallback) |
| Quota utilization | run records `llm_calls` | `docs/monitoring.md` | how close the most recent day is to the documented free-tier cap (`~1500` Gemini RPD) |
| Judge stability | `eval_log.csv` | `docs/monitoring.md` judge table | per-criterion mean + variance on unchanged regression cases, below-3 rate (PRD §401) |
| Cron liveness | healthchecks.io | healthchecks.io | a missed or failed daily run (no-news alert by 8:30 ET) |
| PWA reachability | UptimeRobot | uptimerobot.com | the static site is up |

## The free services — setup

All are **opt-in and off by default**. With their env var unset, the code is a pure
no-op (it does not even construct a request), so nothing here is required for tests or for a
local run. Turn each on when you're ready to operate.

### 1. ~~Sentry~~ — REMOVED 2026-08-06

Deleted rather than left as a dormant option, because it was never going to work and its
presence implied a safety net that did not exist:

* the `[monitoring]` extra was **never installed** — every workflow runs bare `pip install -e .`,
  so `init_sentry()` returned False on every run even though `SENTRY_DSN` was being passed;
* the PWA's DSN line sat **commented out**, so `monitoring.js` returned at line 12, always.

More fundamentally it was the wrong instrument. Every dominant failure in this system is an
**absence** — the cron did not fire, it self-skipped, a source silently degraded, a briefing
published a fallback — and an exception tracker is structurally blind to absence. The pipeline is
also built to **never raise** (`observability`'s non-negotiable), which leaves an exception
tracker nothing to see by construction. healthchecks.io catches absence; that is why it stayed.

### 2. healthchecks.io (free) — cron liveness (catches a dropped / late run)

**Use CRON mode, not a simple "period".** The cron runs TWICE daily at uneven spacing (~10:45 ET
AM, ~17:30 ET PM → a ~16h overnight gap, ~7h daytime gap). A plain period check would false-alarm
every night during the overnight gap. healthchecks.io **cron mode** is schedule-aware — it only
expects a ping at the scheduled times, so a missed session alerts *without* overnight false alarms.
This is the exact failure that bit us **2026-06-22**: GitHub silently dropped the entire AM session
(zero runs fired — `schedule:` triggers are best-effort), so the dashboard froze on the prior day's
read with no alert. A cron-mode check would have emailed by ~18:15 UTC.

1. Create a check (e.g. `macro-daily-briefing`); set **Schedule = Cron**:
   - **Cron expression:** `25 13,21 * * *` — the slots sit **before** the earliest ping either
     session can produce (Worker dispatches 13:45 → publish ~13:46; 21:30 → ~21:32).
     **This ordering is mandatory, not cosmetic.** Cron mode re-arms on every ping: the next
     deadline becomes the first slot *strictly after* the ping received. A ping that arrives
     before its own slot therefore **arms** that slot instead of closing it, and the session —
     already published — never pings again, so the check goes DOWN *because the run was on time*.
     The original `15 14,21 * * *` did exactly this: the 13:46 AM publish armed 14:15, and
     `Publish Quality` + `Data Sources` paged at 18:15 UTC on **2026-07-29** with
     `Last Ping Type: Success`. Any future edit must keep every slot earlier than the earliest
     possible ping, in **both** EDT and EST (EST primaries are 14:45 / 22:30 UTC).
   - **Timezone:** UTC
   - **Grace time:** **5 hours** — absorbs GitHub's habitual ~1–2.5h scheduled-cron delay.
     Grace only ever covers *lateness*. If a check pages while the run was **early**, widening the
     grace cannot fix it — the deadline being extended belongs to a slot the run already passed.
     Move the slot instead.
2. Notifications: email is on by default for the account; add Slack/SMS/etc. on the check if wanted.
3. Copy the check's **ping URL** (`https://hc-ping.com/<uuid>`) and set it as the cron secret:
   `gh secret set HEALTHCHECKS_URL --repo Arash-yazdani/Economy-Dashboard --body "<ping URL>"`
4. No code wiring needed — `scripts/run_daily.py` already brackets every run:
   `ping_healthcheck("start")` → `("success")` on a published outcome → `("fail")` on FRED-down /
   crash (`/start`, `` bare, `/fail` suffixes). Only an **off-window** firing returns before the
   ping; the already-published de-dupe path *does* ping success (`run_daily.py:64`, deliberate —
   see the 2026-06-22 note there), so `HEALTHCHECKS_URL` receives one ping per in-window firing,
   not one per session. The named `publish-quality` / `data-sources` checks are the per-session
   ones: `report_run_health` runs only on a real publish, so they get exactly one ping per session
   and have no buffer pings to mask a mis-specified slot.
   A dropped or failed run ⇒ no success ping ⇒ healthchecks.io alerts at the grace deadline.

### 3. UptimeRobot (free) — PWA reachability

Add an **HTTP(s) monitor** on the production PWA URL (Cloudflare Pages, per ADR-001). No code
change — it probes the public site directly. 5-minute interval is within the free tier.

## Alerting channel

`observability.send_alert(message)` posts `{"text": message}` to `ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK`.

- **Primary — Slack incoming webhook:** create an incoming webhook for a personal channel,
  put the URL in `ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK`. Used by `run_briefing.py`'s top-level crash handler
  and available to the cron entrypoint for a red-dashboard alert.
- **Documented alternative — Gmail SMTP:** if you'd rather email than Slack, point the alert
  sink at a tiny SMTP sender (Gmail app password) instead of the webhook. Not wired in V1; the
  webhook is the V1 default because it's a single env var and no credentials at rest.

Unset webhook ⇒ `send_alert` is a no-op (returns `False`, sends nothing).

## Langfuse (optional, not yet wired)

PRD §397 lists Langfuse free tier (≤50k events/mo — far above our ~365 briefings/yr) as an
optional LLM-trace store. **Not wired in V1.** If added later, it would sit alongside the
JSONL audit log, not replace it (the JSONL log is the §339 system of record). Track as a
V2 nice-to-have.

## Env-var table

| Var | Service | Unset behavior | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HEALTHCHECKS_URL` | healthchecks.io | no cron ping (no-op, no request) | `ping_healthcheck` |
| `ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK` | Slack | no alerts (no-op, no request) | `send_alert` |

See `.env.example` for the copy-paste block. All three are optional; **unset = feature off**.

## Regenerating the dashboard

```bash
python scripts/build_monitoring.py            # reads logs/runs.jsonl + eval_log.csv -> docs/monitoring.md
# prints "STATUS: GREEN" (exit 0) or "STATUS: RED" (exit 3 — cron should pause)
```

Flags: `--runs`, `--eval`, `--runbook` (this file), `--out`, `--window-days` (default 30),
`--now`. Missing/corrupt data files are tolerated (skipped lines, empty inputs), so the
dashboard renders honestly even before the first production run (it says "no production runs
logged yet").

## When it goes red — triage

1. Open `docs/monitoring.md`; read the `STATUS:` banner and `red_reasons`.
2. Identify the failing critical check (`O5` / `O8`) and pull the offending runs from
   `logs/runs.jsonl` (filter on `validator_failed`).
3. **Pause the cron** (the exit-3 gate; or disable the workflow) until fixed.
4. File an incident in [`docs/incidents/`](incidents/README.md) (PRD §339) and follow the
   triage→fix→ship→close loop (PRD §395: re-green the 12-case regression with C2=5/5 and
   C6=5/5 before re-enabling).

## Judge monitoring (PRD §401)

The judge model is monitored alongside the production model. `dashboard.aggregate_judge`
reports, per criterion (`c1`,`c3`,`c4`,`c5`), the **mean and variance** of scores on the
unchanged regression cases, the **below-3 rate**, the latest-run means, and the number of
distinct judge runs. **Score variance creeping up on cases that did not change** is the
instability signal — it triggers a **judge re-prompt** (re-lock `judge.py`'s prompt, re-run
the regression). Cohen's **κ** needs a human-label column not yet present in `eval_log.csv`,
so the dashboard reports `kappa: pending` until that column lands.
